packageRules.description: pnpm/npm override entries (pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, package.json pnpm.overrides/overrides) are hand-authored security remediations keyed by version *selector*, not package name -- e.g. "yaml@1": "1.10.3" means 'consumers resolving into the yaml v1 line get this patched v1', not a package literally named yaml@1. Renovate misreads the selector as a literal package name and proposes cross-major bumps that invert the override's purpose (observed breaking multiple consumer repos: TypeError: expand is not a function from brace-expansion@2->^5, TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'bind') from js-yaml ^3->^5, runtime breakage from minimatch 3.1.5->10.2.6). It also rewrites floor+cap ranges into bare caps (e.g. immutable: >=4.3.9 <5 -> <6), dropping the security floor that justified the override. Suppress majors here: minor/patch still flow so security floors can be raised, and repo-level vulnerabilityAlerts/osvVulnerabilityAlerts configs bypass packageRules for genuine CVE remediation. Crossing a major on an override band must be done by hand, keeping the floor and verifying the actual transitive consumers -- CI rarely exercises them.
